name: Hunyuan3D-2mv
description: Multi-view to 3D mesh generation using Hunyuan3D-2mv. Takes a tiled image of orthographic views (up to 6: front, left, back, right, top, bottom) and outputs a 3D GLB mesh. Texture is a separate node.
author: iammojogo

params_schema.label: Quality Steps
params_schema.tooltip: Number of shape-generation diffusion steps. Lower = faster (5-10 is turbo territory). Higher = slower but potentially better quality (30 is the standard high-quality setting).

params_schema.label: Input Views
params_schema.tooltip: How many views to use for shape generation (1-6). The bridge auto-detects the grid layout from the image aspect ratio (2x2 for ≤4, 2x3 or 3x2 for 5-6). Reading order: [front, left, back, right, top, bottom].

params_schema.label: Mesh Resolution
params_schema.tooltip: Marching-cubes grid resolution — directly sets face count. Lower = coarser/blockier mesh with fewer faces (and less VRAM). 32 gives ~7-8k faces, ideal for low-end meshes.

params_schema.label: Dual Guidance
params_schema.tooltip: Dual-guidance CFG runs 3 forward passes per step on 6GB. Turn off for speed.

params_schema.label: Image Input Mode
params_schema.tooltip: How to interpret the wired image. 'Single' uses the whole image as one view. 'Tiled' splits a pre-made grid (auto-detects 2x2/2x3/3x2 from aspect ratio). 'Folder' reads images from the folder path below.

params_schema.label: Image Folder
params_schema.tooltip: Only used when Input Mode = 'Image Folder'. Path to a folder of images to auto-tile into a 2x2 grid.

nodes.name: Texture Mesh
nodes.description: Hunyuan3D-2.0 paint pipeline. Takes an input mesh plus reference image(s) you wire in, and textures it via multiview diffusion + bake + inpaint. Inpaint is always on (fills UV gaps that would otherwise leave the mesh black).

params_schema.label: Decimate Faces
params_schema.tooltip: Decimate the mesh to ~N triangles before the paint pipeline's UV-unwrap. Lower = faster/less VRAM.

params_schema.label: Texture Resolution
params_schema.tooltip: Resolution of the baked UV texture atlas. Higher = sharper textures but more VRAM and slower bake. 2048 pairs well with the dense UV packing.

params_schema.label: Reference Images
params_schema.tooltip: How many reference views you have wired in, in reading order (front, left, back, right, top, bottom). 1 = whole image as a single front reference. The diffusion model is only ever conditioned on the FRONT view (that is its trained mode; extra views corrupted it). In Hybrid/Deform mode every one of these references is still used: each is warped pixel-exact onto the mesh's silhouette from its matching camera and baked at full resolution, so more real reference views = more of the mesh covered by genuine photo detail instead of diffusion guesswork.

params_schema.label: Delight (Lighting Normalize)
params_schema.tooltip: Remove all shadows and highlights from the reference image before texturing. Includes aggressive flattening to produce a pure albedo with no directional lighting. Strongly recommended for PBR workflows.

params_schema.label: Texture Diffusion Steps
params_schema.tooltip: Number of multiview diffusion steps for texture generation. Lower = faster but less refined. Higher = slower but potentially sharper. 30 is the stock default.

params_schema.label: Image Input Mode
params_schema.tooltip: How to interpret the wired conditioning image. 'Single' uses the whole image as one reference. 'Tiled' splits a pre-made grid (auto-detects 2x2/2x3/3x2 from aspect ratio). 'Folder' reads images from the folder path below.

params_schema.label: Image Folder
params_schema.tooltip: Only used when Input Mode = 'Image Folder'. Path to a folder of images to auto-tile into a 2x2 grid.

params_schema.label: Texture Method

options.label: Hybrid (real pixels on referenced views + diffusion elsewhere)

params_schema.tooltip: How to generate the texture views that get baked onto the mesh. 'Diffusion' runs Hunyuan3D-2 multiview diffusion (single front reference, 512px views; the model synthesizes every other view). 'Hybrid' runs the same diffusion for top/bottom, but every view you have a real reference for (MV-Adapter grid, image folder) is instead pixel-warped onto the mesh's rendered silhouette with a smooth thin-plate spline and baked at FULL resolution — real photo detail, no diffusion smearing, no invented panels. Best used with orthographic multiview references (e.g. the MV-Adapter grid).

nodes.name: Apply Texture
nodes.description: Maps texture atlas image(s) onto a mesh that already has UV coordinates and exports a PBR GLB (albedo + normal + metallic/roughness). Point Texture Folder at your maps or wire the albedo image in. Missing maps are skipped (non-fatal). No diffusion, no bake.

params_schema.label: Mode
params_schema.tooltip: PBR reads normal/roughness/metallic from Texture Folder (or explicit paths) into glTF slots. Albedo only maps the wired image and ignores all map settings.

params_schema.label: Albedo Source
params_schema.tooltip: Wired image input uses the wired image as albedo (folder texturemap ignored). Folder texturemap ignores the wired image and uses texturemap from the folder.

params_schema.label: Texture Folder
params_schema.tooltip: Folder with your PBR maps, found by filename: texturemap (albedo), normalmap, roughnessmap, metallicmap. Maps that don't exist are skipped (non-fatal). If no maps found, output is partial_pbr_mesh.glb.

params_schema.label: Normal Scale
params_schema.tooltip: glTF normalTexture strength. Lower flattens the normal effect, higher exaggerates it.

params_schema.label: Flip Normal Y
params_schema.tooltip: Flip the normal map green channel. Turn On if your maps were authored for DirectX (green-down).

params_schema.label: Smooth Normals
params_schema.tooltip: Average vertex normals across faces so the mesh looks smooth/curved without adding geometry. Turn Off to keep flat/faceted normals.
